used.how: a prepared launch on 32 chips costs ~70-100 us whatever it does, and only folding into a program that already runs removes it: the region / ring copies went into the window send's own prepared program instead of a new prepared copy op
per-chip arg bytes are the launch's host cost: chose 1 copy core (fused call 74 us) over 4 / 8 cores (96 / 123 us) after the probe; the region segment frozen, only the ring pieces as value slots
the copy kernel's args are fixed slots (io addresses, core index, 1 + RING_PIECES segments of 3), no variable-length list; unused ring pieces sent as n = 0
the fused program is prepared once on shape (lazily, first call) and every io address (region, tail, rows, ring) is patched per call; no buffer allocated mid-forward
started from a launch census (op x section x call site per layer, tests/test_attn_launch_census.py) instead of device time, as the census lesson says
P.57's fix list item 6 (attention-side launch cuts) and its per-op us a call were the starting estimate
host per chunk compared on alternating sides (census4: legacy, on, legacy, on) and per call by medians, not one pass a side

missing: prepared_program: PreparedProgram.patch_count also counts the value slots of every core (2016 = 32 x (15 io + 48 value)); the README says only that value slots are never matched to io addresses

overseer.evidence: no padding or duplicated work: unused ring pieces carry n = 0 and copy nothing; the copy kernel moves exactly the rows the legacy slice / slice_write ops moved (tests/test_window_write_fused.py, every chip byte-equal)

the fused window write is built once and dispatched through ttnn.bringup.prepare_program / run_prepared with value_slots (tt/window_send.WindowSend.fused); host 74 us a call (probe) / 86-150 us in the model; no other Python-built op touched, none non-prepared

no fork unit or regression suite run on the 8x4; only the new tests (test_window_write_fused.py, test_attn_launch_census.py) and the model-level checks (measure determinism / quick / p51200, gate unit test_moe_prev_replicas)
